item.title: Lekompo and maskandi to take centre stage at ARMC 2026
item.description: Two distinctly South African sounds will be in focus at this year’s Africa Rising Music Conference (ARMC), returning to Constitution Hill, Johannesburg, on 22 and 23 May. The conference will highlight lekompo and maskandi, genres deeply rooted in local communities but increasingly reaching wider audiences through streaming platforms. item.title: Abigail Chams: Power, purpose and pop
item.description: By Tshifhiwa Mungoni and Sibongile Kobo Tanzania’s rising global star, Abigail Chams is hitting the ground running with a bold dancefloor anthem. Making waves in the local and international music industry with every single that she releases, Chams spotlights her rising influence, her groundbreaking VISA partnership, and the empowering artistic vision behind her single, ‘Your Loss’. item.title: SA: PLUM share new single How The West Was Lost
item.description: By Mzwandile September, Omphile Motlhaping, Shaked Khuzwayo, Bracha Motlhahledi and Musa Songo South African alternative band PLUM has released a new single, ‘How The West Was Lost’, via Mongrel Records, marking the group’s latest output following their return to recording after a lengthy hiatus. Formed in 1996, PLUM built a reputation for working outside rigid genre boundaries. item.title: The Milk Closing Festival scheduled for 28 Feb in Cape Town
item.description: The Milk Closing Festival is set to take place at Khayelitsha Stadium, in Cape Town, South Africa, on 28 February, with organisers confirming a full-day programme running from 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. According to information released by the organisers, the event will feature a large multi-genre line-up of South African artists and DJs. item.title: Open call: SAMRO 2026 Music Publisher Programme
item.description: The Southern African Music Rights Organisation (SAMRO) has opened applications for its 2026 Music Business Lab (MBL) Publisher Programme, a professional development initiative aimed at strengthening music publishing capacity within South Africa’s music sector. item.title: AmaGroove announces line-up for 2026 residency in SA
item.description: One Groove has revealed the official line-up for the 2026 AmaGroove Residency, scheduled to take place at the Kromdraai Impact & Co-Creativity Hub in South Africa from 22 to 29 March. Now in its third year, the residency brings together international artists, producers, vocalists, and songwriters for collaborative sessions, cultural exchange, and music innovation. item.title: Nokuthula Fundama shares new EP ahead of free Heritage concert in Joburg
item.description: By Tshifhiwa Mungoni, Sibongile Kobo, Axolile Lucky Mke, Lucky Maile and Lebogang Masilela South African artist Nokuthula Fundama has released her new EP, Siyaphambili, now available on all major streaming platforms. The project has received positive attention across various media outlets, highlighting Fundama’s ongoing influence as both a recording and performing artist. item.title: SA: Just Bheki’s feature on Emanonini hits over one million streams
item.description: By Matlhodi Molokomme and Lerato Mpho Ramogase South African vocalist, songwriter, and dancer Just Bheki has been credited for his performance on Zani’s latest single, ‘Emanonini’, which has exceeded one million streams across digital platforms. Born in KwaMashu, Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, Just Bheki has built a multi-faceted career as a vocalist, composer, and award-winning dancer. item.title: Music Business Academy to host workshop on distribution, publishing
item.description: The Music Business Academy (MBA), in partnership with SAMRO, will host a workshop in Sandton, Johannesburg on 26 February. The event will focus on music distribution, publishing, and Artists & Repertoire (A&R). The session will bring emerging practitioners into direct engagement with industry executives. item.title: Montreux Jazz Festival launches first African edition in SA
item.description: The Montreux Jazz Festival will make its African debut in Franschhoek, South Africa from 27 to 29 March, featuring a diverse line-up of African legends, international stars and emerging talent. The festival is held annually in Montreux, Switzerland, in early July along the shores of Lake Geneva. It is the world’s second-largest annual jazz festival, after the Montreal International Jazz Festival in Canada.
